name: Matbench v0.1 log_kvrh
description: Predict the base-10 logarithm of the bulk modulus of a crystal (Voigt-Reuss-Hill average in GPa, calculated by density functional theory) from its crystal structure (Matbench v0.1 task log_kvrh, 10987 samples). The evaluation uses the five official folds: for every fold the candidate is called once, in a separate process, with the other four folds and their target values as training data, and must predict the held-out fold within 300 seconds.

Dunn et al. (2020), Benchmarking materials property prediction methods: the Matbench test set and Automatminer reference algorithm (npj Comput Mater): benchmark paper defining the tasks, the nested cross-validation and the metrics; Crossref title verified.

requirements.datasets: matbench_log_kvrh.json.gz from ml.materialsproject.org, folds from the official validation file

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) numbers. Every input is a dict with the keys lattice (the three lattice vectors in angstrom, a 3 x 3 list), species (the element symbol of every site) and frac_coords (the fractional coordinates of every site). info has task, input_type, target, unit, fold, n_train and n_test. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out mean absolute error, minimized.

science_relevance.reason: Each cited paper has the prediction of the task's materials property from composition or structure as its main objective; the Matbench paper is a benchmark paper and is listed under extra_sources only.
science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict the base-10 logarithm of the DFT Voigt-Reuss-Hill bulk modulus (GPa) of an inorganic crystal from its structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: The bulk modulus measures resistance to compression and underlies the design of hard and stiff materials, while DFT elastic calculations are costly, so a learned predictor screens large structure sets.
